question: How does cultural background typically influence a patient's basic human needs?

options.A: It shapes dietary practices, modesty, and views on health
options.B: Culture has no impact on health preferences
options.C: It dictates the exact vital sign ranges for all people
options.D: Culture only affects psychological self-actualization

explanation: Culture strongly guides how individuals view health, express pain, and practice dietary or personal habits. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why must you respect the 'wet contact time' when using a disinfectant?

options.A: Wet surfaces look cleaner to patients and visiting family members
options.B: Water helps the active ingredient evaporate faster to save cleaning time
options.C: Keeping the surface wet prevents dust from settling on medical equipment
options.D: The chemical needs adequate time to interact with and destroy microbial structures

explanation: Disinfection isn't instant magic; it's a chemical reaction! Wiping it dry too soon cuts the process short and lets germs survive.

question: What is the primary purpose of a health care budget?

options.A: To eliminate all unexpected hospital expenses permanently
options.B: To calculate exact salaries for individual doctors and nurses
options.C: To plan and control financial resources for medical services
options.D: To set the retail prices of medications in the pharmacy

explanation: A health care budget serves as a financial plan to guide how money is spent on patient care services. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why must community members be involved in a community diagnosis?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the local government entirely
options.B: To ensure health programs fit their local culture and needs
options.C: To provide financial funding for hospital construction
options.D: To train as professional medical doctors in the village

explanation: Involving the community helps nurses understand local beliefs and realities, making health interventions much more acceptable and successful. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h1)

question: About how fast does rapid-acting insulin start working after you inject it?

options.A: 10 to 15 minutes
options.B: 4 to 6 hours
options.C: 1 to 2 hours
options.D: 12 to 24 hours

explanation: Spot on! Rapid-acting insulin starts working almost immediately, which is why patients need to have their food ready right away.

question: Why do HMOs place a strong emphasis on preventive health services?

options.A: To increase the out-of-pocket bills for the enrollees
options.B: To comply with international travel regulations
options.C: To force patients to visit doctors every single week
options.D: To catch illnesses early and lower expensive treatment costs

explanation: Preventing diseases or treating them early is much cheaper for the HMO than paying for complex, prolonged hospital admissions later. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is the most important advice a nurse should give a patient taking a multi-week course of antifungal drugs?

options.A: Double the next dose whenever a single daily dose is accidentally missed
options.B: Take the pills only on days when itching or burning becomes severe
options.C: Complete the entire prescribed course even if symptoms disappear early
options.D: Stop the medication immediately if mild skin dryness or nausea occurs

explanation: You nailed it! Stopping early is the number one reason fungal infections bounce right back. Always encourage patients to finish the full dose.

question: What is a core duty of a community health nurse during immunization outreach?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines locally
options.B: Tracking local child growth charts
options.C: Performing major surgeries
options.D: Ordering hospital meal trays

explanation: Immunization clinics provide a great opportunity for community nurses to screen children and track their growth patterns. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h2)

question: Which of these medications would you NOT give directly into the heart muscle for routine pain relief?

options.A: Calcium chloride
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Morphine sulfate
options.D: Atropine

explanation: Morphine is a pain reliever (analgesic), not a cardiac arrest drug. It is never poked straight into the heart muscle!

question: Why is it so nutritious to eat beans alongside maize or rice?

options.A: It achieves protein complementation by supplying all essential amino acids
options.B: It doubles the carbohydrate content without adding protein
options.C: It speeds up digestion so the stomach empties faster
options.D: It removes all toxic elements from the beans

explanation: Plant foods often lack one or two building blocks, but combining them (like beans and rice) covers all the bases to make a complete protein!

question: What type of lubricant should always be used on a flatus tube before insertion?

options.A: Water-soluble lubricant
options.B: Sterile cooking oil
options.C: Petroleum-based jelly
options.D: Alcohol-based gel

explanation: Water-soluble lubricant is safe for mucous membranes and prevents trauma, unlike petroleum-based products which are harder to clear and can damage tissues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: In which patient situation is an expectorant the absolute best choice?

options.A: Bacterial pneumonia requiring broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
options.B: A dry, irritating nighttime cough that keeps the patient awake
options.C: Acute bronchitis with thick, difficult-to-cough-up phlegm
options.D: Severe bronchospasm during an acute asthma attack

explanation: Correct! When a patient has heavy bronchitis with stubborn, thick phlegm stuck in their chest, an expectorant is just what they need.

question: What is a key part of a safe emergency obstetric referral from a community clinic?

options.A: Ensuring a trained health worker accompanies the patient
options.B: Sending the patient alone with a family member only
options.C: Withholding all intravenous fluids during transit
options.D: Waiting until daylight before arranging any travel

explanation: Brilliant! Having a trained provider ride along means vital signs are watched and complications like bleeding or seizures can be managed on the way. Teamwork saves lives!

question: What is the primary goal of microbial identification in a clinical setting?

options.A: To count the total number of human cells in a clinical sample
options.B: To measure the patient's exact blood pressure and pulse rate
options.C: To sterilize medical equipment before a surgical procedure
options.D: To determine the exact pathogen causing an infection for targeted treatment

explanation: Knowing the specific organism allows healthcare providers to choose the most effective and narrow-spectrum treatment possible. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h1)

question: In community health nursing, what do we mean by a "food taboo"?

options.A: A cultural rule against eating certain foods
options.B: A government law controlling food prices
options.C: A medical prescription for weight loss
options.D: An allergic reaction to specific meals

explanation: A food taboo is simply a cultural or religious rule that says 'no' to eating certain edible items. You'll see this often in community postings!

question: Why does quickly sorting (triage) a coughing patient help stop airborne infections in a crowded clinic?

options.A: It isolates infectious individuals away from the general waiting crowd
options.B: It eliminates the need for any staff personal protective equipment
options.C: It immediately cures the underlying respiratory infection
options.D: It guarantees that laboratory test results return within minutes

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! Spotting coughing patients early and moving them away from other waiting patients stops germs from spreading in the waiting room.

question: Why should you wear heavy-duty utility gloves instead of thin examination gloves when carrying waste bags?

options.A: They provide greater puncture and tear resistance against hidden sharp objects
options.B: They prevent hands from sweating in hot tropical weather
options.C: They allow healthcare workers to touch patient wounds directly
options.D: They are cheaper to purchase in large wholesale quantities

explanation: Utility gloves are thick and tough. They act as a strong physical barrier against stray needles or sharp trash that might poke through thin exam gloves.

question: What should a unit manager do when staff members have a workplace conflict?

options.A: Reporting both workers to the police immediately
options.B: Acting as a mediator to restore a collaborative working relationship
options.C: Taking sides with the senior doctor against the nurses
options.D: Encouraging the staff members to stop speaking entirely

explanation: Great job! A good manager steps in to help sort out friction, keeping the team united and the working environment safe for everyone.

question: Why shouldn't you fill a sharps container past its fill line?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from recycling the plastic material
options.B: It makes the container too heavy for the waste collectors
options.C: It increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: It causes the plastic walls of the container to melt

explanation: You got it! Overfilling sharps bins means needles start poking out or pushing against the lid, putting anyone handling the bin at high risk of a needle-stick injury.

question: Why is it dangerous to press down on a waste bag with your hands to create more space?

options.A: It causes hidden sharps to puncture your skin
options.B: It breaks the plastic bag open and makes a mess
options.C: It ruins the color-coding system of the bin
options.D: It releases unpleasant odors into the ward

explanation: People often throw away loose needles or broken glass illegally into soft bags, and pressing down pushes those items right into your hand. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h5)

question: Which of these weight changes is considered a major red flag during a nutritional check-up?

options.A: Involuntary loss of 10 percent of body weight over six months
options.B: Gradual weight gain due to reduced physical activity
options.C: A stable weight fluctuating by one kilogram each week
options.D: A slight increase in body mass index after recovering from an illness

explanation: Spot on! Losing 10% or more of body weight in half a year is a serious warning sign of nutritional decline that requires immediate nursing attention.

question: As a nurse, what major emotional or psychological challenge should you anticipate for a patient facing a radical hysterectomy?

options.A: Complete loss of long-term memory function
options.B: Sudden denial of the physical diagnosis by family members
options.C: Intense fear of hospital food and environmental sounds
options.D: Body image disturbance and grief over lost fertility

explanation: Spot on. Losing reproductive organs can trigger profound emotional grief regarding womanhood, body image, and the ability to have children. Compassionate nursing support is everything here.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand a patient's cultural or religious food practices?

options.A: It guarantees that the patient will never develop chronic illnesses
options.B: It helps create realistic and acceptable dietary plans the patient will actually follow
options.C: It allows the nurse to change the patient's cultural beliefs to match hospital standards
options.D: It is only required for legal documentation and has no clinical value

explanation: Dietary recommendations that clash with a patient's cultural or religious values are rarely sustained at home. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h5)

question: What happens if a bar chart's vertical scale doesn't start at zero?

options.A: The categories on the horizontal axis automatically disappear
options.B: The chart becomes a continuous line graph instead
options.C: Small differences between groups can look exaggerated and misleading
options.D: The total number of patients surveyed is cut in half

explanation: Starting a Y-axis above zero can play tricks on the eyes, making tiny gaps look like massive clinical differences. Always check that scale!

question: Why are healthcare-associated infections a major concern in nursing?

options.A: They prolong hospital stays and increase patient suffering
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for antibiotics
options.C: They only affect nurses who fail to wear gloves
options.D: They are caused exclusively by patient diet changes

explanation: Infections acquired during healthcare delivery add heavy burdens to patients by worsening their health and lengthening their recovery time. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h1)

question: When a person suddenly faces a scary or stressful situation, what is the first stage of the body's stress response called?

options.A: Alarm reaction
options.B: Exhaustion phase
options.C: Recovery period
options.D: Resistance stage

explanation: That sudden rush you feel when startled? That's the alarm reaction! It's your body's immediate fight-or-flight kick-start to help you handle sudden stress. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h1)

question: How do community health nurses bridge the gap between workers and management?

options.A: By advocating for safe practices and helping design workable health policies
options.B: By taking over management duties and running the factory business
options.C: By hiding workplace injuries so the company looks good
options.D: By convincing workers to ignore safety rules to save money

explanation: Nurses act as advocates and educators, helping both sides understand that worker safety benefits everyone. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)

question: Which human sense is widely believed to be the absolute last to fade before a patient dies?

options.A: Hearing
options.B: Touch
options.C: Sight
options.D: Taste

explanation: Hearing usually stays intact longer than other senses. That's why we always encourage families to keep talking and comforting their loved ones right up until the end. Beautiful nursing knowledge!

question: What is one effective nursing action during a multidisciplinary ward round?

options.A: Writing new drug orders without consulting the attending doctor
options.B: Hiding the prescription chart from the medical team
options.C: Discharging all patients who take more than two tablets daily
options.D: Questioning unnecessary prescriptions and suggesting alternatives

explanation: Nurses act as safety advocates by speaking up when a medication order appears unsafe or clinically unjustified. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the emergency procedure where a tiny cut is made in the neck membrane to open a blocked airway?

options.A: Removing a tracheostomy tube
options.B: Bronchoscopy
options.C: Cricothyroidotomy
options.D: Thoracentesis

explanation: A cricothyroidotomy is an emergency lifesaving move. When nothing else works and the upper airway is fully shut, healthcare providers cut through the cricothyroid membrane to create a direct path for air.

question: What is the highest number of skin patches a patient can have to be classified as having paucibacillary leprosy?

options.A: 2 patches
options.B: 20 patches
options.C: 5 patches
options.D: 10 patches

explanation: Paucibacillary simply means 'few bacteria.' Clinically, it's marked by having between one and five skin patches. You're doing great!

question: A 14-year-old pregnant patient faces a high nutritional risk. Why does this happen during her pregnancy?

options.A: Complete resistance to iron supplementation
options.B: Direct competition for nutrients between her growing body and the fetus
options.C: Permanent storage overload of water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Immediate cessation of all bone mineral absorption

explanation: Exactly! Since a young teenager is still growing herself, her body and the baby have to share and compete for limited nutrients.

question: What are the tiny spaces inside bone tissue where mature bone cells live called?

options.A: Lacunae
options.B: Osteons
options.C: Lamellae
options.D: Trabeculae

explanation: Great try! Lacunae are like tiny little hotel rooms nestled inside the hard bone matrix where bone cells (osteocytes) hang out and maintain the tissue.

question: Which organelle is responsible for producing most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP?

options.A: Lysosome
options.B: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
options.C: Golgi apparatus
options.D: Mitochondria

explanation: Mitochondria convert nutrients into usable cellular energy (ATP), earning them the title of cellular powerhouses. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why should a research report use clear and simple language?

options.A: Busy healthcare workers must easily understand and apply the findings
options.B: Journals will reject any paper that uses simple everyday language
options.C: Patients require the full report to manage their own treatments
options.D: Medical terminology is banned in modern academic publishing

explanation: Wards are busy places! Clear writing helps nurses quickly grab key facts and use them at the bedside.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of simple pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Worsening discomfort after eating a large meal
options.B: A sour taste at the back of the throat
options.C: A burning feeling behind the breastbone
options.D: Crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw

explanation: Crushing jaw pain points toward heart trouble, not regular acid reflux. Good clinical spotting!

question: What is a major, life-altering complication frequently linked to advanced endometriosis?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Infertility
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Systemic hypertension

explanation: Due to scarring and ongoing inflammation, getting pregnant can become a real hurdle for many women battling advanced endometriosis.

question: How does putting perishable food in the fridge right away help protect health?

options.A: It turns raw ingredients into ready-to-eat meals
options.B: It completely kills all existing viruses in meat
options.C: It slows down bacterial multiplication in perishable foods
options.D: It removes chemical toxins from spoiled vegetables

explanation: Brilliant! Fridges don't kill bacteria, but the cold temperature acts like a brake, slowing down how fast those tiny germs can grow and multiply.

question: What is the primary purpose of a research proposal?

options.A: To summarize the final conclusions of a completed study
options.B: To publish patient case studies in a medical journal
options.C: To outline a planned study before collecting data
options.D: To evaluate the daily performance of hospital staff

explanation: A research proposal acts as a blueprint prepared before any investigation starts. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h1)

question: A student wants to study 'hospital stress'. Which option is a well-focused, realistic research topic?

options.A: Reviewing the history of global healthcare systems
options.B: Comparing the salaries of all hospital workers worldwide
options.C: Assessing night-shift burnout among intensive care unit nurses
options.D: Finding out why people get stressed in all buildings

explanation: Great research topics are narrow and specific! Focusing on a particular group (ICU nurses) and issue (night-shift burnout) makes your study much easier to manage.

question: Which spinal nerve roots give rise to the nerves of the pelvic floor?

options.A: T10 to L1
options.B: S2 to S4
options.C: L1 to L3
options.D: C1 to C3

explanation: Correct! Remember 'S2, 3, 4 keeps the pelvic floor off the floor!' A handy little trick for your exams.

question: What should health education focus on most for younger primary school children?

options.A: Advanced reproductive physiology and anatomy
options.B: Occupational hazard management in industries
options.C: Basic hygiene like handwashing and dental care
options.D: Chronic disease pharmacology and medication doses

explanation: Correct! Little ones benefit the most from mastering everyday self-care routines that keep common germs away.

question: What does 'shared decision-making' mean in nursing?

options.A: The patient deciding on treatments without any input from healthcare staff
options.B: The nurse making all clinical choices based solely on hospital policy
options.C: Family members making all health choices on behalf of the patient
options.D: Collaboration between the nurse and patient using clinical expertise and personal values

explanation: You got it! It's a true partnership where professional medical knowledge meets the patient's personal life values.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of left-sided heart failure?

options.A: Enlarged and tender liver
options.B: Shortness of breath and crackles in the lungs
options.C: Visible bulging of the neck veins
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: When the left side of the heart struggles, blood backs up into the lungs, causing fluid buildup, breathlessness, and lung crackles.

question: How does severe poverty make it much harder for someone to escape an abusive relationship?

options.A: It stops community members from offering emotional comfort
options.B: It prevents healthcare facilities from providing physical examinations
options.C: It creates financial dependence that makes leaving the abuser extremely difficult
options.D: It automatically removes all legal rights from the victim in court

explanation: Spot on! Without personal money or shelter, many survivors feel stuck because they simply cannot afford basic survival necessities on their own.

question: What is the main drawback of a positive Mantoux (tuberculin skin) test?

options.A: It cannot distinguish between latent and active infection
options.B: It only works in patients who have never received vaccinations
options.C: It is completely unreliable for diagnosing immunocompromised adults
options.D: It requires laboratory analysis of blood within two hours

explanation: A positive skin test simply means your immune system has seen TB before. It cannot tell if the infection is sleeping (latent) or active.

question: Why should a nurse avoid going back to alter past chart entries after a bad patient event?

options.A: Electronic health records automatically freeze all keyboards for 48 hours after an incident
options.B: Altering records can be perceived in court as an attempt to cover up a mistake or hide negligence
options.C: State board regulations require nurses to write all documentation on paper instead
options.D: Hospital billing software will reject the patient's insurance claim if a note is edited

explanation: Tampering with charts destroys your credibility in court. If something was missed, follow your facility's protocol for late entries instead of trying to cover it up!

question: What is key to getting staff members to gladly accept a newly introduced management decision?

options.A: Immediate disciplinary action for anyone who asks questions
options.B: Clear communication of the reasons behind the change
options.C: Changing the shift roster every single day without notice
options.D: Keeping all details of the new policy hidden from view

explanation: When nurses understand the 'why' behind a new policy, they are far more likely to support it and work together.

question: What is the main purpose of connecting family caregivers with respite care services?

options.A: To train them to become licensed professional registered nurses
options.B: To replace the primary doctor during medical emergencies
options.C: To lower the financial cost of purchasing prescription medications
options.D: To give them temporary relief and prevent physical or emotional exhaustion

explanation: Respite care offers temporary breaks for family members, protecting them from caregiver burnout. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a 'just culture' in healthcare?

options.A: Punishing all clinical errors with immediate suspension from work
options.B: Encouraging open reporting by separating honest mistakes from recklessness
options.C: Ensuring that every staff member receives the exact same salary
options.D: Removing all rules and regulations so staff can work freely

explanation: A just culture supports safety by welcoming error reports and understanding that honest mistakes are different from intentional reckless acts.

question: Where should the surgical needle be grasped by the needle holder?

options.A: At the extreme tail end of the thread
options.B: One-third to one-half from the swaged end
options.C: Right at the very sharp point of the needle
options.D: Directly in the exact middle of the curve

explanation: Holding the needle at this position gives the best balance of control and prevents the needle from bending or breaking. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why do you need to watch the needle site extra carefully after drawing blood from someone with severe liver disease?

options.A: Their veins are usually completely collapsed from chronic fluid overload
options.B: Their skin is too fragile to tolerate standard adhesive tape
options.C: They often have poor clotting due to low production of clotting factors
options.D: Local anesthetics used during the draw can cause severe allergic reactions

explanation: You nailed it! A struggling liver can't pump out enough clotting proteins, meaning your patient is at a higher risk of prolonged bleeding or bruising after a needle stick.

question: Which heart rate pattern on a monitor is most commonly associated with uteroplacental insufficiency?

options.A: Early accelerations
options.B: Short-term skips
options.C: Baseline variability
options.D: Late decelerations

explanation: Late decelerations begin after a contraction starts and return to baseline only after it ends, showing that the baby cannot handle the reduced oxygen during contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h3)

question: Why do our cells constantly need metabolic processes?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for intravenous fluids
options.B: They maintain basic life functions and support tissue repair
options.C: They regulate blood pressure by controlling kidney size
options.D: They prevent all forms of bacterial and viral infections

explanation: Cells are tiny powerhouses! They rely on ongoing metabolism to make energy, heal wounds, and keep your body running smoothly every single day.

question: Which living condition makes the rapid spread of airborne respiratory infections much easier?

options.A: Overcrowded housing with poor ventilation
options.B: Living in a dry and dusty rural climate
options.C: Residing near a flowing freshwater river
options.D: Consuming food cooked over open firewood

explanation: Spot on! When people are packed tightly together with stale air, respiratory droplets pass easily from one person to the next.

question: A nurse draws up the wrong dose of a drug but realizes it before giving it to the patient. What do we call this?

options.A: A near miss
options.B: A never event
options.C: An adverse event
options.D: A sentinel event

explanation: Spot on! Because the nurse caught the mistake before administration, the patient was safe. That's a textbook near miss.

question: When is an employer usually NOT held liable for a nurse's action?

options.A: When the nurse engages in a major personal detour from work duties
options.B: When the nurse follows a hospital protocol that contains a minor flaw
options.C: When the nurse makes a standard medication calculation error on the ward
options.D: When the nurse takes a short authorized break inside the hospital building

explanation: If you leave your post to go handle a major personal errand far away, you've stepped outside your job description, and the hospital is off the hook for what happens.

question: Why does the government bother controlling and monitoring health spending?

options.A: To ensure that health workers receive tax exemptions
options.B: To eliminate all private hospitals in the country
options.C: To replace traditional medicine with imported drugs
options.D: To manage limited resources and prevent financial waste

explanation: Money is never unlimited! Governments regulate health spending to make sure public funds are used wisely without unnecessary waste.

question: In community health nursing, what is the main goal of advocacy?

options.A: Protecting and promoting the rights and health of vulnerable populations
options.B: Prescribing medications when doctors are unavailable
options.C: Managing hospital financial records and budgets
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital visitation rules

explanation: Spot on! Advocacy is all about being a voice for people and communities who struggle to speak up for themselves, making sure they get the care and respect they deserve.

question: Which of these choices is a MAJOR safety violation when handling hospital equipment?

options.A: Checking for frayed electrical cords
options.B: Obtaining informed consent from the patient
options.C: Skipping equipment cleaning to save time
options.D: Ensuring proper disinfection between patients

explanation: Never skip cleaning! Proper maintenance and disinfection protect patients from nasty infections and keep equipment running smoothly.

question: A client looks very scared about going to the general hospital to remove a contraceptive implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Cancel the referral and send the client home without protection
options.B: Scold the client for being afraid of a minor procedure
options.C: Tell her that hospitals are terrifying places and she must just endure it
options.D: Listen to her concerns, explain the procedure simply, and reassure her

explanation: Fear is completely normal. Sitting down to listen and breaking down what will happen turns anxiety into confidence.

question: What process does a sublingual drug successfully avoid by entering the bloodstream directly?

options.A: Gastric acid destruction
options.B: First-pass metabolism
options.C: Renal excretion
options.D: Pulmonary filtration

explanation: Great job! Because it skips the liver's initial breakdown (first-pass metabolism), more active drug reaches your patient.

question: In the fast AVPU neurological screening tool, what does the letter 'P' stand for?

options.A: Responds to pain
options.B: Pulse is present
options.C: Patient is paralyzed
options.D: Pupils react

explanation: AVPU is a quick check: Alert, Verbal, Pain, Unresponsive. 'P' means the patient only wakes up or reacts when you apply pain.

question: What is the medical term for excessive thirst experienced by a client with high blood sugar?

options.A: Proteinuria
options.B: Polyuria
options.C: Polyphagia
options.D: Polydipsia

explanation: Polydipsia is the medical word for extreme thirst, which happens because the body loses a lot of water through frequent urination. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h4)

question: How does the work differ between a Senior CHEW and a Junior CHEW?

options.A: Junior CHEWs perform major surgeries, while Seniors only do paperwork
options.B: Senior CHEWs only work in cities, while Juniors work exclusively abroad
options.C: Senior CHEWs handle independent diagnoses and treatments under protocol, while Juniors work under closer supervision
options.D: There is no difference in their training or daily clinical duties

explanation: You got it! Senior CHEWs have extra training that lets them manage common health issues independently using standing orders, while juniors work more closely with supervisors.

question: What happens when food moves way too quickly through a person's colon?

options.A: Ulceration
options.B: Appendicitis
options.C: Diarrhea
options.D: Constipation

explanation: If food rushes through the colon, there's no time to absorb water, leading to loose, watery stools. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: What structure marks the point where nerve fibers exit the eye to form the optic nerve?

options.A: Optic disc
options.B: Pupil
options.C: Retina
options.D: Macula

explanation: The optic disc is the anatomical convergence point where nerve fibers leave the eye and appears as a yellowish-pink structure during the exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h2)

question: A newly bereaved family member sits quietly without crying and says everything is fine. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The person is lying to trick the medical staff
options.B: The person lacks any emotional capacity for love
options.C: The person may be experiencing shock or emotional numbing
options.D: The person has already successfully reached full acceptance

explanation: A lack of tears does not always mean peace; it often indicates emotional shock or denial. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which part of the ear does a tympanic thermometer aim for?

options.A: The sublingual pocket
options.B: The temporal artery
options.C: The tympanic membrane
options.D: The carotid sheath

explanation: Tympanic thermometers go gently into the ear canal to pick up heat coming straight off the eardrum.

question: What is the main use of a run chart in quality improvement?

options.A: To record patient medical diagnoses in an emergency
options.B: To schedule holiday shifts for nurses
options.C: To display data points over time and track performance trends
options.D: To calculate annual salaries for hospital staff

explanation: Spot on! Run charts plot data chronologically so you can see at a glance whether your ward's new interventions are actually improving things.

question: What is the primary goal of government food safety regulations?

options.A: To increase the cost of importing foreign goods
options.B: To prevent foodborne illnesses and contamination
options.C: To make sure all food items taste identical
options.D: To prevent small vendors from selling fresh produce

explanation: Safety regulations protect consumers from harmful biological and chemical agents found in unsafe food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h4)

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear that an IUD will cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Tell the client that her fears are irrational and insist she accepts the device anyway
options.B: Provide calm, evidence-based education explaining that fertility returns immediately upon IUD removal
options.C: Agree that permanent damage is common and suggest she avoids all birth control
options.D: Ignore the comment and document that the client refused all medical advice

explanation: Respectful nursing care involves correcting myths gently with factual information while supporting the client's ultimate autonomy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: What is the main goal of giving a standard clinical vaccine?

options.A: To provide immediate chemical relief from chronic joint inflammation
options.B: To destroy all existing white blood cells in the patient's body
options.C: To permanently block the liver from metabolizing oral medications
options.D: To introduce safe antigens that stimulate long-term memory cells

explanation: Vaccines give a harmless 'practice preview' of an infection so the immune system can build memory cells and protect the patient later.

question: Which body system controls the release of hormones that trigger puberty?

options.A: Hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
options.B: Sympathetic-adrenomedullary pathway
options.C: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
options.D: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system

explanation: Well done! The HPG axis is the body's master control center for releasing the sex hormones that drive all those physical changes during puberty.

question: What should you do if you notice fresh, bright red bleeding from the rectum after a washout?

options.A: Report the finding to the physician immediately
options.B: Document it as a completely normal expected result
options.C: Administer a stronger oral laxative dose to the patient
options.D: Wait twenty-four hours to see if it stops on its own

explanation: Bright red blood means there might be a small injury or tear in the lining. Always let the doctor know right away so it can be checked.

question: Why is independent clinical judgment especially important for a home health nurse?

options.A: Home health clients never require emergency medical intervention
options.B: Hospital protocols do not apply outside formal medical facilities
options.C: Families dictate the exact medical treatments the nurse must perform
options.D: Doctors and other supervisors are not physically present in the home

explanation: Exactly! When you are out in the field visiting a patient's home, you often work solo. Your own assessment skills and quick thinking are key to spotting any health changes. Great job!

question: A community health team wants to know if their new malaria prevention posters were successful. What is the best way to check?

options.A: Ask the local printer if they enjoyed making the colorful graphic designs
options.B: Count how many posters are left neatly stacked inside the nurse's office drawer
options.C: Measure changes in community health habits, such as increased use of insecticide-treated nets
options.D: Assume success because the hospital director liked the color scheme

explanation: The real test of good communication is seeing actual behavior change and healthier habits in the community!

question: Why is it dangerous to give rescue breaths too fast or with too much force?

options.A: It can force air into the stomach and lead to vomiting
options.B: It immediately collapses both lungs due to high pressure
options.C: It causes the patient's heart rate to drop dangerously low
options.D: It forces blood backward into the jugular veins

explanation: Easy does it with breaths! Blowing too hard opens up the stomach instead of the lungs, which can cause the patient to vomit and complicate things.

question: Why might a patient give a vague, unbelievable story about a bad injury during a home visit?

options.A: Hospital guidelines discourage patients from discussing injuries
options.B: Fear of retaliation or shame often prevents them from telling the truth
options.C: Patients with chronic illness rarely remember how they get hurt
options.D: They want to test the clinical diagnostic skills of the nurse

explanation: Spot on. Fear of making things worse at home or feeling embarrassed makes many victims hide what really happened.

question: What are the core parts of comprehensive Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Antibiotic therapy alone without any further clinical follow-up
options.B: Criminal investigation, legal counseling, and mandatory detention
options.C: Surgical sterilization, blood transfusions, and long-term isolation
options.D: Emergency treatment, family planning, and reproductive health linkages

explanation: Wonderful! PAC is a complete package that covers acute medical treatment, birth control counseling, and connection to wider health resources.

question: What does the Phosphatase Test check for during milk processing?

options.A: The exact percentage of fat and protein present
options.B: The total number of live bacteria in the sample
options.C: Whether pasteurization was successfully carried out
options.D: If antibiotics were given to the dairy cattle

explanation: You got it! The enzyme alkaline phosphatase is naturally killed off by proper heating. If the test shows the enzyme is gone, it proves the milk was successfully pasteurized.

question: What is the name of the fluid-filled structure that implants into the lining of the womb?

options.A: Zygote
options.B: Blastocyst
options.C: Gamete
options.D: Morula

explanation: The blastocyst is the gorgeous little ball of cells ready to nestle comfortably into the uterine lining. You're doing brilliantly with these terms!

question: What does Type IV FGM involve?

options.A: Surgical reconstruction of damaged labial tissue
options.B: Pricking, piercing, scraping, or cauterizing the genital area
options.C: Complete removal of the uterus and ovaries
options.D: Routine episiotomy performed during childbirth

explanation: Type IV is the catch-all category for any other harmful, non-medical tinkering with female genitalia. Every question you answer makes you a sharper nurse!

question: How do cultural traditions and religious beliefs affect a family's emotional well-being?

options.A: They guide how the family expresses feelings, handles grief, and looks for help
options.B: They decide what exact medical diagnosis a patient gets
options.C: They completely remove all mental stress
options.D: They stop caregivers from ever feeling tired or burnt out

explanation: Culture and faith are like a lens. They shape how families make sense of sickness, mourn their losses, and decide where to turn for comfort.

question: A pregnant woman's pelvic bones feel slightly loose to help with childbirth. What type of joint is this?

options.A: Diarthrosis
options.B: Fibrous
options.C: Synarthrosis
options.D: Amphiarthrosis

explanation: Wonderful! An amphiarthrosis is a slightly movable joint. Hormones help the pubic symphysis stretch just enough during delivery.

question: What is the very first practical safety step before applying a prepared warm poultice to a patient?

options.A: Wrap the entire body in thick blankets
options.B: Test the temperature of the mixture
options.C: Leave the room for thirty minutes
options.D: Scrub the skin hard with stiff wire wool

explanation: Always test the temperature to prevent accidental burns before the substance touches the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h6)

question: What happens inside the brain when there is a severe shortage of thiamine?

options.A: Nerve cells multiply too fast and form lumps
options.B: Blood vessels in the head become too thick
options.C: Brain cells run out of energy and get damaged or die
options.D: Brain tissue fills up with excess water

explanation: Spot on! Without thiamine, cells can't make energy. This leads to cell stress, bleeding, and eventually cell death.

question: At what stage do primary oocytes pause their development while a baby girl is still in the womb?

options.A: Telophase of mitosis
options.B: Anaphase of meiosis II
options.C: Metaphase of meiosis II
options.D: Prophase of meiosis I

explanation: Think of it like hitting a pause button. Primary oocytes pause in prophase of meiosis I before a baby girl is even born, and they stay paused for years!

question: What is a major immediate health risk associated with sexual violence?

options.A: Permanent loss of hearing capacity due to psychological shock
options.B: Sudden elevation of red blood cells in the circulatory system
options.C: Acquisition of sexually transmitted infections and unwanted pregnancy
options.D: Immediate development of chronic osteoarthritis in the knees

explanation: Sexual assault places victims at immediate risk for physical trauma, sexually transmitted infections, and unwanted pregnancies requiring emergency prophylaxis. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the best way for a nurse leader to handle a transport breakdown during community outreach?

options.A: Wait passively until the government builds a paved highway
options.B: Blame the community members for living in a hard-to-reach area
options.C: Use adaptive problem-solving to find alternative transport methods
options.D: Cancel all future community outreach programs indefinitely

explanation: Great nurses are resourceful! When plans hit a roadblock, we think on our feet and find another way to reach our patients.

question: Which sign tells you a patient has severe malaria instead of just uncomplicated malaria?

options.A: Impaired consciousness or coma
options.B: Loss of appetite
options.C: Mild intermittent headache
options.D: Low-grade joint pain

explanation: Spot on! Any sign of confusion, extreme weakness, or coma (cerebral malaria) means it's an emergency needing immediate inpatient care.

question: What is the standard rule for turning a bed-bound patient to help prevent pressure sores?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: Once per shift
options.D: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: Turning a patient at least every two hours takes the weight off vulnerable spots, giving blood flow a chance to rush back in and save the skin. Simple and life-saving! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: What communication style should a nurse use when counseling a caregiver who defaulted on vaccines?

options.A: Total silence while the caregiver reads a pamphlet
options.B: Rapid medical terminology to prove professional status
options.C: Strict lecturing to show authority and clinical power
options.D: Respectful listening and clear, non-judgmental explanations

explanation: Caregivers respond better to patience and empathy than to strict scolding, which often makes them avoid the clinic permanently. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h5)

question: Where is the best place to keep your sharps disposal box during an injection?

options.A: In the nurse's station for later
options.B: Locked in a store room down the hall
options.C: On the floor right under the patient's bed
options.D: Right within arm's reach of your workspace

explanation: Keep your safety box close! Walking around with an open, used needle just asks for an accidental poke.

question: In a healthcare setting, what does 'resource allocation' mean?

options.A: Calculating the exact profit made by a pharmacy
options.B: The process of admitting patients to private rooms
options.C: Writing new nursing textbooks for students
options.D: How funds, staff, and supplies are distributed

explanation: Great! Resource allocation is simply deciding how to share out available money, materials, and staff to where they are needed most.

question: Why should a community health nurse view the entire community as their 'client'?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to examine individual patients
options.B: Individual health is deeply connected to broader community functions
options.C: Hospital administrators require nurses to count every resident
options.D: Local laws prohibit nurses from treating people one at a time

explanation: Brilliant! Looking at the whole community helps you tackle root issues like poverty, environment, and culture that affect every single patient.

question: Why do single neurons connect with hundreds of other neurons instead of working totally alone?

options.A: To prevent the spread of harmful electrical storms in the spinal cord
options.B: To ensure that sensory messages never reach the motor cortex
options.C: To slow down electrical signals so the brain can rest between tasks
options.D: To allow the body to process simple reflexes and complex thoughts simultaneously

explanation: Neurons love teamwork! By linking up in networks, they help your brain multitask effortlessly—handling quick reflexes and deep thoughts all at once.

question: What is the main benefit of using the teach-back method with a patient?

options.A: It tests the patient's long-term memory from their childhood.
options.B: It replaces the need for any written discharge paperwork.
options.C: It proves to the doctor that the nurse did their job correctly.
options.D: It checks whether the patient truly understood the care instructions.

explanation: You got it! Asking them to explain things back in their own words is the best way to catch any misunderstandings before they go home.

question: What is a major risk if a recovering patient stays on a clear liquid diet for too long?

options.A: It triggers sudden weight gain from excess fats
options.B: It causes severe high blood pressure
options.C: It permanently ruins the patient's sense of taste
options.D: It can lead to hospital-derived malnutrition due to very low calorie and nutrient content

explanation: Clear liquids are great at first, but they don't have enough energy and nutrients. Keeping patients on them too long starves their healing body!

question: What is the primary goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To diagnose and treat chronic adult illnesses
options.B: To provide free accommodation for teachers
options.C: To replace local hospitals within rural communities
options.D: To promote and protect the well-being of students and staff

explanation: The core purpose of the programme is safeguarding the physical, mental, and social health of the school population. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the main job of dietary calcium during the teenage years?

options.A: Enhancing visual acuity
options.B: Regulating blood pressure
options.C: Building peak bone mass
options.D: Preventing adult anemia

explanation: Spot on! The teenage years are the golden window where most of your adult bone strength is locked in. Drink up that milk!

question: What is the main goal of the family planning referral method in community nursing?

options.A: To connect clients to specialized or unavailable reproductive health services
options.B: To permanently discharge clients from primary health care facilities
options.C: To reduce the overall number of children born in a specific community
options.D: To decrease the administrative workload of community health nurses

explanation: Think of a referral as a helpful bridge! When a client needs care or family planning methods that your local clinic cannot provide, you connect them to a place that can.

question: Why do qualitative researchers include direct quotes from participants in their results?

options.A: To let participants speak in their own voices and add authenticity
options.B: To replace the need for any written interpretation or analysis
options.C: To increase the total word count of the research report
options.D: To prove that every participant agreed with the researcher

explanation: Verbatim quotes provide direct evidence of the lived experiences, making the qualitative narrative believable and grounded in reality. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a clinical leader and a clinical manager?

options.A: Leaders focus on inspiring people and driving change, while managers focus on operational systems and stability.
options.B: Leaders handle the payroll and disciplinary actions, while managers take care of patient assessments.
options.C: Leaders rely purely on formal authority, while managers rely solely on personal charisma.
options.D: Leaders work exclusively in outpatient clinics, while managers work only in intensive care units.

explanation: You've got it! Think of managers as keeping the ship running smoothly day-to-day, and leaders as steering the ship toward new horizons.

question: How is a longitudinal study different from a cross-sectional study?

options.A: Cross-sectional studies are always experimental, while longitudinal studies are always observational
options.B: Longitudinal studies use animals, while cross-sectional studies only use human nurses
options.C: Longitudinal studies follow participants over a period, while cross-sectional studies collect data at one single point
options.D: Cross-sectional studies take many years to complete, while longitudinal studies take only one day

explanation: You've got it! Think of a cross-sectional study as a quick one-time photo snapshot, while a longitudinal study is like a video tracking changes over time.

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty?

options.A: Hormonal surges from the endocrine system
options.B: Sudden changes in environmental temperature
options.C: Rapid expansion of skeletal muscle mass
options.D: Increased intake of dietary proteins

explanation: Puberty kicks off when the brain sends signals to the endocrine system to release hormones that drive body changes.

question: Why is a water-soluble lubricant used instead of an oil-based jelly on the tube?

options.A: Water-soluble jelly permanently stiffens the plastic tube
options.B: Oil-based lubricants make the tube too slippery to hold
options.C: Water-soluble jelly will not harm the lungs if accidentally inhaled
options.D: Oil-based products react badly with stomach acid

explanation: If the tube accidentally enters the trachea, a water-soluble lubricant is safely absorbed by lung tissue, unlike oils which cause lipid pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why is it usually a mistake to jump straight into psychological counseling before sorting out a patient's Tier 1 needs?

options.A: Specialized medications will work twice as fast
options.B: The client will automatically recover without needing shelter
options.C: The psychological interventions will likely fail because survival anxiety overrides therapy
options.D: Counseling becomes much more effective because the client focuses inward

explanation: It makes total sense: if a patient is freezing, starving, or scared for their physical life, they cannot focus on talking through emotional trauma.

question: Why shouldn't dietary supplements replace whole foods?

options.A: Supplements are always too expensive for ordinary patients to afford daily
options.B: Whole foods provide a complex balance of nutrients and fiber that isolated supplements lack
options.C: Conventional foods contain prescription drugs that supplements completely lack
options.D: The human digestive tract cannot absorb any chemical compound created in a laboratory

explanation: Real foods give you a rich mix of fiber and interacting nutrients that a single pill just can't copy. Balance is key!

question: What is the main purpose of giving a blood transfusion to a patient with acute haemorrhage?

options.A: To prevent the kidneys from producing any urine
options.B: To speed up the digestion of food in the stomach
options.C: To replace lost red blood cells and restore oxygen delivery
options.D: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature

explanation: Transfusions supply the red blood cells needed to carry oxygen to tissues when the patient's own blood volume is dangerously depleted. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h6)

question: Why are nurses in such a great position to catch adverse drug reactions early?

options.A: They are legally responsible for manufacturing all hospital drugs
options.B: They maintain close, continuous contact with hospitalized patients
options.C: They perform all laboratory blood chemistry tests
options.D: They set the retail prices for pharmaceuticals in Nigeria

explanation: Because you spend the most time right at the bedside, you are usually the first to notice early physical or mood changes after a patient takes a drug.

question: After teaching an insulin-dependent diabetic client how to inject medication at home, what must the nurse document?

options.A: The specific teaching content, the method used, and the client's return demonstration
options.B: Only the date and time of the home visit without mentioning the teaching
options.C: That the client bought an expensive refrigerator for storing the insulin
options.D: That teaching is unnecessary because the client is educated

explanation: Documenting education requires proof of what was taught and how the client showed they understood it. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why do urinary buffers like phosphate and ammonia matter so much when the kidneys excrete acid?

options.A: They prevent water from being reabsorbed in the collecting duct
options.B: They actively transport glucose molecules back into the bloodstream
options.C: They supply the necessary sodium ions for the renin pathway
options.D: They bind free hydrogen ions so urine pH does not drop too low

explanation: Buffers tie up free hydrogen ions like a sponge. This keeps the urine from becoming dangerously acidic, letting the kidneys keep clearing out more acid.

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place during emergency care for severe abortion complications?

options.A: To flush the bladder with antiseptics to kill germs
options.B: To keep the patient from moving around the ward
options.C: To monitor hourly urine output and check kidney function
options.D: To collect a clean urine sample for a routine pregnancy test

explanation: Watching urine output closely tells us if the kidneys are getting enough blood flow while recovering from shock. Excellent clinical tracking!

question: What is the proper way to remove a honeybee stinger stuck in the skin?

options.A: Scrape it gently across the skin using a flat, rigid edge
options.B: Burn the stinger with a heated match to neutralize the venom
options.C: Squeeze the venom sac tightly with metal tweezers and pull straight out
options.D: Scrub the area vigorously with a stiff surgical brush

explanation: Never squeeze a bee stinger! Squeezing pushes more venom into the skin. Instead, gently scrape it away with something flat like a card.

question: Why is 'trial and error' considered a risky problem-solving technique at the bedside?

options.A: It requires permission from the hospital board of directors
options.B: It can cause direct harm to the patient if the first guess is wrong
options.C: It takes too long to document in the hospital computer
options.D: It is completely forbidden by all nursing regulatory councils

explanation: Testing random solutions on a human body can lead to dangerous clinical outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which medication is used in medical abortion to cause strong uterine contractions?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Ergometrine
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Misoprostol helps the uterus contract and safely push out any remaining tissue. You'll see this drug used a lot in ward practice!

question: A community nurse notices a family pulled their 12-year-old daughter out of school while keeping her younger brother in class. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Cultural preference for investing in male education and financial dependence of women
options.B: An official policy granting free education exclusively to male children
options.C: Government regulations prohibiting females from attending secondary school
options.D: Medical evidence showing girls learn better through home apprenticeships

explanation: When money is tight, families with gender bias often sacrifice a daughter's schooling to pay for the son's. As nurses, spotting these patterns helps us guide the family better.

question: Why is female genital mutilation (FGM) traditionally performed?

options.A: To prevent severe pelvic infections in young girls
options.B: To enhance natural hormonal balance during puberty
options.C: To treat congenital reproductive disorders
options.D: To comply with non-medical cultural and social beliefs

explanation: Spot on! FGM is done for cultural or social reasons, not for any medical treatment or health benefit. You've got this!

question: What core belief describes a patriarchal system when it comes to early marriage?

options.A: Young girls should lead community governance councils.
options.B: Females hold less social value and personal autonomy than males.
options.C: Fathers have no legal authority over their children's marital choices.
options.D: Both parents share equal decision-making power over household finances.

explanation: You nailed it. In patriarchal setups, power rests mainly with men, which unfortunately strips women and girls of their right to make personal life choices.

question: What does it mean when a drug like phenytoin has a 'narrow therapeutic index'?

options.A: The drug only works on a tiny, specific area of the brain
options.B: Patients must only take the medication once every few weeks
options.C: The drug cannot be absorbed if taken with food in the stomach
options.D: The difference between a safe dose and a toxic dose is very small

explanation: A narrow therapeutic index means we have to walk a tightrope! Too little drug and the seizures return; too much and the patient gets toxic. That's why blood level checks are so crucial.

question: How often should a bedbound patient ideally be repositioned to prevent pressure injuries?

options.A: Only when the patient complains
options.B: Once every twelve hours
options.C: At least every two hours
options.D: Once per day during the morning shift

explanation: Turning or repositioning a patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on vulnerable skin areas and tissues. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h6)

question: Damage to which part of the brain is primarily responsible for the balance and coordination problems seen in ataxic cerebral palsy?

options.A: Brainstem
options.B: Basal ganglia
options.C: Motor cortex
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: The cerebellum is the main brain structure that regulates balance, posture, and coordinated movement. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why are individuals with pre-existing mental health conditions especially vulnerable during disasters?

options.A: They are completely immune to physical injuries
options.B: Disasters automatically cure their psychiatric symptoms
options.C: Their usual support systems and medication routines are often disrupted
options.D: Emergency workers always prioritize them over everyone else

explanation: When clinics close, pharmacies run out of stock, and daily structures collapse, stable mental health conditions can quickly deteriorate. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h4)

question: An unconscious patient arrives at the emergency unit after a head injury and cannot manage their own saliva. What is the main reason to put them on a ventilator?

options.A: Lowering body temperature
options.B: Airway protection
options.C: Treating high blood pressure
options.D: Correcting severe anemia

explanation: When someone is unconscious, they lose reflexes like swallowing and coughing. Putting them on a ventilator protects their airway so they don't aspirate secretions into their lungs. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: Which of these snacks is safest to give a toddler just as it is, without cutting it first?

options.A: A handful of roasted peanuts
options.B: Thinly sliced soft banana pieces
options.C: A whole hard candy lozenge
options.D: Whole raw baby carrots

explanation: Well done! Soft bananas mash up easily and don't pose the hard, sticky, or round risks that nuts, carrots, or candies do.

question: Where should the toxic ash from burning medical waste be dumped?

options.A: Shallow trenches dug right behind the hospital
options.B: Open community rubbish pits near local farms
options.C: Secure engineered landfills with protective liners
options.D: Standard municipal recycling bins for plastic

explanation: Incinerator ash has chemicals and toxins in it, so it must go into a specially lined landfill to protect our soil and drinking water.

question: Why is it important to respect a patient's cultural background when planning their meals?

options.A: Because medical science proves cultural foods are superior
options.B: To prevent the client from ever eating carbohydrates
options.C: Because hospital policy strictly forbids serving foreign foods
options.D: To ensure the client is willing and able to follow the meal plan long-term

explanation: People eat what they love! When we respect cultural food preferences, patients are much more likely to stick to their diet.

question: What is a very common challenge when trying to introduce quality improvement in a busy Nigerian ward?

options.A: Staff burnout and resistance to new routines
options.B: Patients demanding too many safety checklists
options.C: An excess of extra nursing staff on every shift
options.D: Doctors writing too many clear care instructions

explanation: So true! When nurses are already tired and overworked from busy shifts, asking them to learn brand new routines can be tough. We have to support each other!

question: What is the most common cause of rectovaginal fistula in developing countries?

options.A: Bladder stones
options.B: Hormonal imbalances
options.C: Chronic appendicitis
options.D: Prolonged and obstructed labor

explanation: Prolonged pressure from the baby's head against the pelvis causes tissue ischemia and necrosis, leading to fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: Why do doctors prescribe medications for heart failure if they don't completely cure the disease?

options.A: To reduce heart workload and slow disease progression
options.B: To replace the need for dietary sodium restriction
options.C: To permanently repair damaged heart valve tissue
options.D: To cure the underlying viral infection in the muscle

explanation: Great thinking! Since heart muscle doesn't easily repair itself, these drugs are lifesavers because they make the heart's job much easier and help patients live longer, more comfortable lives.

question: What is the best imaging test to check for liver hydatid cysts?

options.A: Electrocardiography
options.B: X-ray fluoroscopy
options.C: Ultrasound
options.D: Positron emission tomography

explanation: Ultrasound is safe and brilliant at spotting fluid-filled cysts hiding inside the liver.

question: What makes the Vagus nerve (Cranial Nerve X) stand out from most other cranial nerves?

options.A: It controls the sense of smell entirely on its own.
options.B: It has no sensory function whatsoever.
options.C: It travels all the way down into the chest and tummy.
options.D: It only activates during high stress or panic.

explanation: Fantastic! While most cranial nerves stay around the head, the vagus nerve wanders down to supply our chest and belly organs.

question: A woman who underwent FGM as a child is admitted in active labor. What is she at higher risk for during delivery?

options.A: Rapid, painless delivery due to relaxed pelvic muscles
options.B: Obstructed labor and severe tearing from scar tissue
options.C: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.D: Instant healing of the perineal area after birth

question: Which ethical principle directly supports a competent patient's right to refuse medical treatment?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Justice

explanation: Autonomy is the ethical principle that respects an individual's right to make independent choices about their own body and healthcare. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is a major financial advantage of home health care over hospital admission?

options.A: It avoids expensive daily hospital room charges and facility overhead costs
options.B: It guarantees a monthly financial stipend for the patient's family
options.C: It makes all medical supplies and prescription drugs completely free
options.D: It removes the need for health insurance policies entirely

explanation: Eliminating hospital room and board fees significantly lowers the overall cost of treatment. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the main shift that occurs during an epidemiological transition?

options.A: A shift from infectious diseases to chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: A shift from high birth rates to zero population growth
options.C: A shift from urban living to rural farming settlements
options.D: A shift from hospital care to traditional healing practices

explanation: As societies develop and life expectancy increases, the primary health burden moves away from acute infections toward chronic lifestyle and age-related illnesses. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which ethical rule guides how resources are shared when supplies are very scarce during a disaster?

options.A: Giving the newest supplies only to wealthy donors
options.B: Treating every person strictly on a first-come, first-served basis
options.C: Justice and doing the greatest good for the greatest number
options.D: Refusing care until formal legal contracts are signed

explanation: You've got it! In mass disasters, we shift from treating just one person to figuring out how to do the greatest good for the whole community fairly.

question: Which of these are classified as micronutrients?

options.A: Carbohydrates and water
options.B: Fibers and amino acids
options.C: Proteins and fats
options.D: Vitamins and minerals

question: A mother believes her child's fever is caused by witchcraft rather than malaria, and avoids the clinic. What is the best way for a nurse to respond?

options.B: Scold the mother for holding backward beliefs that put her child in mortal danger
options.C: Call the local security forces to force the mother to accept malaria medication

explanation: Good nursing means meeting patients where they are. Building trust and respecting cultural concerns helps us guide patients toward safe, proven treatments.

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.B: Safety, Behaviour, Assessment, Review
options.C: Staff, Budget, Action, Report
options.D: Symptoms, Bedside, Analysis, Recovery

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's bedside locker to clear out old, forgotten food brought by family?

options.A: Perishable foods lose all their carbohydrate value within two hours
options.B: Hospital policy forbids patients from eating food brought by relatives
options.C: Unrefrigerated perishable food breeds bacteria that cause food poisoning

question: In mass casualty triage, what does a RED tag mean?

options.A: Minor cuts and bruises that can be treated with basic self-care methods
options.B: Immediate, life-threatening injuries requiring urgent intervention to save life
options.C: Stable injuries that can safely wait several hours for medical attention
options.D: Catastrophic injuries where the patient has little chance of survival

explanation: Red means 'Right now!' These patients have severe, life-threatening injuries and need our immediate care to survive.

question: Which of the following is a key criterion used to prioritize community health problems?

options.A: Distance from the capital city international airport
options.B: Magnitude or number of people affected
options.C: The political party affiliation of the village head
options.D: The architectural design of the local health clinic

explanation: Magnitude measures how widespread a health issue is, helping planners focus on problems affecting the largest segments of the population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the dorsal root ganglion?

options.A: It generates motor commands for reflex actions
options.B: It connects the spinal nerve directly to the sympathetic trunk
options.C: It produces cerebrospinal fluid to cushion the nerve
options.D: It houses the cell bodies of sensory neurons

question: Which specific part of the penis contains and surrounds the urethra?

options.A: Glans penis
options.B: Crura of the penis

options.D: Corpus cavernosum

question: An audit shows nurses forget pain scores because the chart has no space for them. What is the best fix?

options.A: Suspending every nurse working on the ward without pay
options.B: Banning the use of all written documents on the hospital ward
options.C: Telling patients they must diagnose their own pain levels
options.D: Redesigning the pain chart to include a clear, dedicated space for scores

question: Which part of the spinal cord controls the parasympathetic signals needed for an erection?

options.A: T1 to T4
options.B: L1 to L3
options.C: S2 to S4
options.D: C1 to C3

question: Who are considered key stakeholders when mobilizing a Nigerian community for a public health campaign?

options.A: Only the youngest children in the primary school
options.B: Foreign tourists visiting local wildlife parks
options.C: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and local group heads
options.D: International manufacturing companies overseas

question: What is the main advantage of facility-based quarantine over home quarantine for arriving travelers?

options.A: It allows quarantined persons to continue going to their normal workplaces.
options.B: It removes the need for any infection control supplies whatsoever.
options.C: It guarantees that travelers will never catch any other illness.
options.D: It allows health workers to monitor symptoms and test individuals more easily.

explanation: Centralized facilities allow medical staff to perform regular temperature checks and administer diagnostic tests efficiently. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the main job of flat bones in the body?

options.A: Absorbing high impact forces in tight spaces like the wrist
options.B: Acting as long levers to propel the body forward during running
options.C: Guiding tendons smoothly across major joints without friction
options.D: Protecting internal organs and providing broad muscle attachment sites

explanation: Flat bones (like your skull and sternum) act like helmets and shields for vital organs while giving muscles a wide place to anchor.

question: A ward manager wants to speed up patient discharges. Using systems thinking, what is the best first step?

options.A: Examine how nursing, pharmacy, and transport work together during discharge
options.B: Force the nursing staff to work faster without talking to others
options.C: Focus only on speeding up the discharge lounge staff
options.D: Punish nurses whose patients take too long to leave

explanation: To fix a delay, you have to look at the whole chain of events, not just one group of workers.

question: What is an example of secondary epidemiologic data?

options.A: Measuring the mid-upper arm circumference of children
options.B: Interviewing village elders about local health beliefs
options.C: Conducting blood pressure checks at a local market square
options.D: Reviewing past mortality records from the health ministry

question: Why do nurses monitor blood tests like prealbumin during high calorie therapy?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of urine produced daily
options.B: To determine the patient's current level of physical pain
options.C: To check how well the body is processing and storing nutrients
options.D: To screen for underlying genetic disorders

explanation: Blood proteins like prealbumin change quickly when nutritional status improves, helping us see if our nutrition plan is hitting the mark.

question: What is the hallmark warning sign of placenta previa?

options.A: Painless, bright red vaginal bleeding
options.B: Sudden swelling of the face and hands
options.C: High fever and foul-smelling discharge
options.D: Severe sharp pain with a rigid abdomen

question: What happens when surviving nephrons have to overwork because their neighbors broke down?

options.A: They regenerate completely to cure the disease
options.B: They stop working immediately to rest the kidney
options.C: They turn into normal liver cells
options.D: They undergo hyperfiltration and suffer further damage

question: Where must the traction weight bags always be positioned?

options.A: Tied tightly to the metal headboard of the bed
options.B: Supported on a small stool placed next to the bed
options.C: Resting securely on the bottom mattress for safety
options.D: Hanging freely without touching the floor or bed frame

question: Why should you call or alert the receiving hospital before the patient physically arrives?

options.A: To allow the specialist team time to prepare necessary equipment and space
options.B: To prevent the patient from changing their mind during transit
options.C: To give the nurse permission to leave the clinic early
options.D: To ensure the hospital bed fee is paid in advance by mobile money

explanation: Spot on! Calling ahead gives the emergency or specialist team precious time to ready their staff, drugs, and equipment before the patient rolls in.

question: Who must give consent if a research study involves confused elderly patients?

options.A: Legally authorized representatives
options.B: The head hospital security guard
options.C: Any nurse working on the shift
options.D: The pharmaceutical company sponsor

explanation: Well done! When patients can't speak for themselves, we rely on their trusted representatives to protect their rights and safety.

question: Why should you always share your assessment findings back with the community members who helped you?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to write clinical notes
options.B: It builds trust and encourages active community commitment
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting the clinic again
options.D: It is required to collect fines from households

explanation: Sharing your findings shows respect for their time and input, and it makes them proud partners in solving their own health challenges!

question: How can a nurse best support a burnt-out family caregiver who is stressed about feeding duties?

options.A: Blaming the caregiver for the patient's poor nutritional status
options.B: Telling the caregiver to stop worrying and let the patient starve
options.C: Taking over all household chores permanently without involving family
options.D: Connecting caregivers with respite care and community support resources

explanation: Caregivers need a break too! Linking them with support and respite care helps them rest so they can continue providing great care safely.

question: How do cultural traditions in Nigeria often influence end-of-life care preferences?

options.A: Family members are legally barred from participating in bedside care
options.B: Families often prefer patients to spend their final days at home surrounded by relatives
options.C: Traditional practices completely replace all modern nursing interventions
options.D: Patients almost always request solitary care in private hospital rooms

explanation: In many Nigerian communities, passing on surrounded by family at home is a deeply cherished tradition, bringing great comfort to everyone involved.

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when collecting data for an explanatory study?

options.B: Using standardized scales for every single participating subject

question: What is the main focus of a national nursing organization like NANNM?

options.A: Country-specific labor laws and domestic health policies
options.B: Directing medical research for pharmaceutical corporations
options.C: Global monetary funds for hospital construction worldwide
options.D: Setting international travel guidelines for nurse migration

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the popular BRAIDED counseling mnemonic?

options.A: Billing

options.D: Benefits

question: Why is oophoritis rarely found completely by itself in the clinic?

options.C: It usually spreads to the fallopian tubes and nearby pelvic organs

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of strong teamwork among healthcare professionals in the community?

options.A: Better sharing of critical clinical updates

question: Which mental health condition is common in women experiencing flashbacks and severe anxiety linked to FGM trauma?

options.A: Schizophrenia
